Water and TiCl₄, each computed with the same input in ORCA and in Gaussian 16. The Gaussian route
contains `iop(6/80=1)`, so both programs print Löwdin charges. A second Gaussian water job differs only in
the d/f functions (Cartesian 6D 10F instead of pure 5D 7F), which shows how sensitive both schemes are
to the basis set.

**Files used** (from the repository):

* `tests/data/gaussian_ref/orca/g01_h2o_pure.out` — ORCA, B3LYP/def2-TZVPP, H₂O
* `tests/data/gaussian_ref/gaussian/g01_h2o_pure.log` — Gaussian 16 twin, `5D 7F pop=full iop(3/33=1) iop(6/80=1)`
* `tests/data/gaussian_ref/gaussian/g02_h2o_cart.log` — Gaussian 16, same job with Cartesian `6D 10F` functions
* `tests/data/gaussian_ref/orca/g04_ticl4.out` — ORCA, B3LYP/def2-TZVP, TiCl₄ (Gaussian twin `gaussian/g04_ticl4.log`)

**1. Atoms 0 and 1 in four files** (0-based: O and H in water, Ti and one Cl in TiCl₄).

```bash
frog-charges tests/data/gaussian_ref/orca/g01_h2o_pure.out tests/data/gaussian_ref/gaussian/g01_h2o_pure.log tests/data/gaussian_ref/orca/g04_ticl4.out tests/data/gaussian_ref/gaussian/g04_ticl4.log -i 0 1
```

```text
ℹ  Processing: tests/data/gaussian_ref/orca/g01_h2o_pure.out
ℹ  Processing: tests/data/gaussian_ref/gaussian/g01_h2o_pure.log
ℹ  Processing: tests/data/gaussian_ref/orca/g04_ticl4.out
ℹ  Processing: tests/data/gaussian_ref/gaussian/g04_ticl4.log
                                              Charges (Mulliken and Löwdin)
╭───────────────────────────────────────────────────┬───────┬─────────────┬───────────┬───────┬─────────────┬───────────╮
│ File                                              │ #0 El │ #0 Mulliken │ #0 Löwdin │ #1 El │ #1 Mulliken │ #1 Löwdin │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────┼─────────────┼───────────┼───────┼─────────────┼───────────┤
│ tests/data/gaussian_ref/orca/g01_h2o_pure.out     │ O     │      -0.389 │     0.289 │ H     │       0.194 │    -0.144 │
│ tests/data/gaussian_ref/gaussian/g01_h2o_pure.log │ O     │      -0.389 │     0.289 │ H     │       0.194 │    -0.144 │
│ tests/data/gaussian_ref/orca/g04_ticl4.out        │ Ti    │       1.082 │    -0.807 │ Cl    │      -0.271 │     0.202 │
│ tests/data/gaussian_ref/gaussian/g04_ticl4.log    │ Ti    │       1.082 │    -0.807 │ Cl    │      -0.271 │     0.202 │
╰───────────────────────────────────────────────────┴───────┴─────────────┴───────────┴───────┴─────────────┴───────────╯
```

* ORCA and Gaussian print the same charges for the same job.
* Mulliken gives the chemically expected signs: O −0.389 / H +0.194 and Ti +1.082 / Cl −0.271.
  **Löwdin reverses both signs** in these large, polarised basis sets: O +0.289 / H −0.144 and Ti −0.807 /
  Cl +0.202. This is what the programs print, not a parsing error. It shows why neither scheme should be
  read as an absolute charge.

**2. Same molecule, different basis-function type.** Only the d/f functions change (pure → Cartesian).
The CSV output keeps all six decimals.

```bash
frog-charges tests/data/gaussian_ref/gaussian/g01_h2o_pure.log tests/data/gaussian_ref/gaussian/g02_h2o_cart.log -i 0 --format csv -q
```

```text
# Charges (Mulliken and Löwdin)
File,#0 El,#0 Mulliken,#0 Löwdin
tests/data/gaussian_ref/gaussian/g01_h2o_pure.log,O,-0.388889,0.288605
tests/data/gaussian_ref/gaussian/g02_h2o_cart.log,O,-0.358343,0.116563
```

The oxygen Mulliken charge moves from −0.388889 to −0.358343, and the Löwdin charge from +0.288605 to
+0.116563. The geometry and functional are the same. Compare charges only within one basis set, and use NPA
(`frog-nbo --npa`) when a less basis-dependent number is needed.
